# target_ct bytes from 0x402060, 27 bytes
target_ct = bytes([0x8b, 0x5f, 0x1e, 0xe7, 0x9c, 0x11, 0xa1, 0x28, 
                   0xde, 0x77, 0xe8, 0x98, 0x17, 0x88, 0x5a, 0xc3,
                   0x77, 0x03, 0x82, 0x37, 0xd2, 0x43, 0x43, 0x87, 
                   0xd4, 0x29, 0x30])

# Starting counter is 0xffffffcd, but we work with bytes (mod 256)
# The algorithm checks: input[i] XOR (counter & 0xff) == target_ct[i]
# Then counter = counter + input[i]

# Starting value 0xffffffcd as a signed int wraps to 0xCD (205) when masked to 8 bits
counter = 0xffffffcd

result = []
for i in range(27):
    # Get low byte of counter for XOR
    counter_byte = counter & 0xff
    # input[i] = target_ct[i] XOR counter_byte
    c = target_ct[i] ^ counter_byte
    result.append(c)
    # Update counter: add input character
    counter = (counter + c) & 0xffffffff  # Keep as 32-bit

decoded = bytes(result)
print("Decoded input:", decoded)
print("As string:", decoded.decode('utf-8', errors='replace'))
